s0301.literal: Father Pu inherited the fief and served Wu, reaching Administrator of Zangke.
s0301.idiomatic: His father Min Pu inherited the title, served Eastern Wu, and rose to governor of Zangke.

s0302.literal: Zuan sojourned south of the river in Henan Xin'an; in youth he roamed among heroes and made many alliances; he read widely in the classical tomes and comprehended the patterns of things.
s0302.idiomatic: Min Zuan had settled south of the Yellow River in Xin'an, ran with bold company in his youth, and read his way through the canon until the world's workings made sense to him.

s0303.literal: When father died, the stepmother was not kind; Zuan served her with reverence ever more meticulously.
s0303.idiomatic: After his father died, his stepmother turned cold; he only served her with tighter courtesy.

s0304.literal: Yet mother hated him yet more severely; then falsely accused Zuan of stealing father's-time gold and jewels, and litigated him before the responsible offices.
s0304.idiomatic: She grew crueler still: she invented a theft of his father's old treasures and dragged him before the magistrates.

s0305.literal: Thereupon he bore pure-reputation condemnation over ten years; Zuan showed no colour of resentment, filial-care reverence without slackening.
s0305.idiomatic: For more than a decade the gossip of the Nine Ranks ruined him anyway; he never wore resentment on his face and never slacked as a son.

s0306.literal: Mother afterward intention resolved; further shifted Central Rectifier; then obtained restored rating.
s0306.idiomatic: When she relented at last and the Central Rectifier was replaced, his rank could be restored.

s0307.literal: Became retainer to Grand Tutor Yang Jun, transferred to magistrate of Anfu.
s0307.idiomatic: He entered Yang Jun's household as a retainer, then was rotated out as magistrate of Anfu.

s0308.literal: At Jun's execution, Zuan abandoned office and returned, importuned Jun's former chief clerk Pan Yue, aide Cui Ji, et al., jointly to bury him.
s0308.idiomatic: When Yang Jun fell, Zuan resigned and went home, then pressed Yang's old chief clerk Pan Yue, aide Cui Ji, and others into giving him a decent burial.

s0309.literal: Ji, Yue feared crime; pushed Zuan to be chief.
s0309.idiomatic: Cui and Pan were terrified of guilt and pushed Zuan to lead the affair.

s0310.literal: Tomb completed, when time to bury, Jun's cousin Mo reported to Prince Dan of Wuling, intending memorialize killing those who conceived the scheme.
s0310.idiomatic: The grave was nearly ready when Yang Jun's cousin Yang Mo told Prince Dan of Wuling he would memorialize for the execution of whoever had dreamed up the burial.

s0311.literal: All alike feared, filled mound and fled; Zuan alone with family wealth completed tomb, buried Jun and departed.
s0311.idiomatic: The company panicked, shoveled earth in panic, and scattered; Zuan alone spent his own fortune to finish the work, buried Yang Jun, and walked away.

s0312.literal: Libationer of the National Academy Zou Zhan deemed Zuan's talent fit assistant composition, recommended him to Librarian-in-Chief Hua Qiao.
s0312.idiomatic: Zou Zhan, libationer of the academy, thought Zuan could help compile the histories and commended him to Hua Qiao, the librarian-in-chief.

s0313.literal: Qiao said: 'This duty is idle, granary-grain heavy; noble power much contends it; no leisure to seek its talent.
s0313.idiomatic: Hua Qiao answered, 'That chair pays well for light work—every powerful family squabbles for it. Nobody has time to ask whether anyone there can write.'

s0314.idiomatic: So he never took him on.

s0315.literal: Prince Yong of Hejian drew him as marshal to the Colonel of Western Rong; had merit; enfeoffed Marquis of Pingle township.
s0315.idiomatic: Prince Yong of Hejian recruited him as army marshal under the western frontier colonel; he earned merit and received the village marquisate of Pingle.

s0316.literal: At Crown Prince Minhuai's deposition, Zuan bore coffin arrived at palace gate, submitted memorial sorting crown prince's wrong, saying:
s0316.idiomatic: When Crown Prince Minhuai was deposed, Zuan shouldered a coffin to the palace gate and filed a memorial to clear Sima Yu's name. It read:

s0317.literal: Prostrate I have seen amnesty text and posted-below former crown prince Yu's own draft; I deemed it shock.
s0317.idiomatic: I have read the amnesty edict and the former crown prince's plea, posted beneath it, and I am stunned.

s0318.literal: From antiquity, minister-son rebellions, never had like this extreme.
s0318.idiomatic: In all of history no subject or son's revolt has ever cut this deep.

s0319.literal: Fortunately rely Heaven's kindness, preserve complete his head-neck.
s0319.idiomatic: Only Heaven's mercy has spared his life.

s0320.literal: Your servant prostrate reflects: Yu born of sage father yet reached here, from being long reared deep palace, sunk in wealth-nobility, received surplus late emperor, father-mother spoiled him.
s0320.idiomatic: Your servant believes Yu was sired by a sage-king yet came to this because he was raised behind high walls, drowned in luxury, pampered by the late emperor, and indulged by his parents.

s0321.literal: Each time I see selection from tutors down to crowd clerks, generally take fat-grain strike-bell tripod-eat households, rarely have cold-gate Confucian-plain like Wei Wan, Zhou Wen, Shi Fen, Shu Guang; tutor-in-attendance, retainer likewise have no Ji An, Zheng Zhuang comparison; thereby caused not to see serving-father serving-ruler Way.
s0321.idiomatic: Look at everyone from his tutors down to clerks: they are almost always plutocrats who dine to the chime of bells. You never see poor scholars like Wei Wan, Zhou Wen, Shi Fen, or Shu Guang, nor stewards comparable to Ji An or Zheng Zhuang—so he never learned how to obey a father or a sovereign.

s0322.literal: Your servant cases classical models: crown prince dwells by knight ritual, ranks with state's people—by this clarify former kings wished make him know first low afterward then noble.
s0322.idiomatic: The canon says an heir should live by the rites of a knight and stand in line with commoners—precisely so a king teaches him humility before greatness.

s0323.literal: Since lately Eastern Palace likewise slightly too flourishing, that by which brought defeat.
s0323.idiomatic: Lately the Eastern Palace has itself swelled beyond measure—that is why it collapsed.

s0324.literal: Not only Eastern Palace: surveying kings' tutor-friends literature, all powerful clans strength can obtain, generally not Gong Sui, Wang Yang, able by Way to instruct.
s0324.idiomatic: And it is not only the heir: every prince's friends and literary advisers are bought with clan muscle. Few are another Gong Sui or Wang Yang who could teach the Way.

s0325.literal: Friends lack bright-straight three-benefits integrity; office by literature as name, truly not read books, only together fine clothes good horses, release wine high feasts, sport-travel chess-betting—how have polish-debate, able mutually grow benefit!
s0325.idiomatic: Those 'friends' lack the stern friendship the Master praised. Offices called 'literary' never open a book; they flaunt silks and horses, throw roaring parties, dice, and hunts. Where is honest argument to sharpen character?

s0326.literal: Your servant constantly fears ducal clans slack-decay; by this sigh.
s0326.idiomatic: I have long dreaded the wasting of the imperial house—and this is why I sigh.

s0327.literal: Now Yu may take as warning; fear his being cast-off, abandoned driven far outskirts, beginning then repent faults, nothing again reach.
s0327.idiomatic: Let Yu serve as warning. If you cast him out to some border post, he may repent when nothing can be salvaged.

s0328.literal: Formerly Rebel Heir misbehaved, raised arms resist mandate; yet Huguan three-old submitted memorial, had Tian Qianqiu's words, still said: 'Son played father's arms, crime should birching ear!
s0328.idiomatic: Prince Ju of Han still rose in arms against his father, yet the elder of Huguan reminded the throne that a son who borrows his father's army deserves only a flogging.'

s0329.literal: Han Wu took it to heart, built Thinking-Son terrace.
s0329.idiomatic: Emperor Wu listened and raised the Terrace for the Longing Son.

s0330.literal: Now Yu misbehaves, speech rebellious; receiving crime days, dare not lose Way; still lighter than Rebel Heir, still can restrain-hold, heavily reselect guardian-tutors.
s0330.idiomatic: Yu has misbehaved and his language was treasonous, yet when sentence came he kept his bearing—still a lighter case than Prince Ju. He can be held in check if you choose new guardians and tutors with care.

s0331.literal: Such as Minister of Works Zhang Hua, virtue-morality deep far, heart loyal-sincere—take him as tutor.
s0331.idiomatic: Minister of Works Zhang Hua has profound virtue and a loyal heart—name him senior tutor.

s0332.literal: Grand Master of Splendid Brightness Liu Shi, cold-bitter self-stood, end-beginning not decline, age same Lü Wang, classics not abandoned—take him as guardian.
s0332.idiomatic: Grand Master of Splendid Brightness Liu Shi rose from hardship without bowing; he matches Lü Wang in years and never sets the classics aside—name him guardian.

s0333.literal: Vice Minister of Masters of Writing Pei Wei, bright-trustworthy reverent-stern, embody Way dwell correct—take him as friend.
s0333.idiomatic: Vice Minister Pei Wei is lucid, honest, and grave, and he walks the straight path—name him companion-adviser.

s0334.literal: Set wandering-talk literature, all select cold-gate orphan-office those by learning-conduct self-stood, and take wear-diligence change-affairs, tread-travel hardship-danger, serve-ruler serve-kin, name-conduct plain-heard, make with them dwell together.
s0334.idiomatic: Fill the 'literary' slots with poor-born officials who live by scholarship, and add men hardened by real service—men known for serving ruler and family through trouble—and let them room with him.

s0335.literal: Make stern censor supervise-guard his house, cut off noble-kin sons-young, frivolous guests.
s0335.idiomatic: Put a strict censor over his household and shut out noble boys and flashy guests.

s0336.literal: Like this left-right front-rear, none not correct men.
s0336.idiomatic: Then whoever stands near him morning and night will be upright.

s0337.literal: Tutor-guardian literature, can order tenth-day one lecture, make together debate discourse before.
s0337.idiomatic: Have tutors and literary officers lecture once every ten days and argue policy in front of him.

s0338.literal: Ordered agents only discourse ancient-modern filial sons kind-parents, loyal ministers serve ruler, and think-fault mend-pass meaning—all hear good Way, perhaps nearly can preserve whole.
s0338.idiomatic: Tell them to speak only of filial sons, faithful ministers, and how to reckon with sin and mend it—pour good counsel into his ears until something takes root.

s0339.literal: Formerly Tai Jia had crime, banished three years, thought ordinary able restore, became Yin enlightened king.
s0339.idiomatic: Tai Jia offended his ministers and spent three years in exile pondering duty; when he returned he became a worthy king of Shang.

s0340.literal: Further Wei Emperor Wen feared at seeing abolish; early-night self-watchful; in end able self-preserve-complete.
s0340.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Wei lived in dread of deposition, disciplined himself night and day, and survived.

s0341.literal: Reaching Emperor Ming—because mother got crime—demoted Plains Marquis—set retainers heir-trainees, tutor-friends literature, all taken correct men, together mutually rectify-straight.
s0341.idiomatic: Emperor Ming of Wei was stripped to marquis of the plain when his mother fell; handlers gave him steward, tutors, companions, and literary aides—all upright men—to steady one another.

s0342.literal: Fearful-fearful careful punishment; serve father with filial; father deceased, serve mother with care; heard throughout Under Heaven—unto today praises him.
s0342.idiomatic: He threaded every danger with caution, honoured his father in life and nursed his mother after—stories everyone still repeats.

s0343.literal: Han High Emperor repeatedly set ale in courtyard, wished abolish crown prince; afterward Four Hoary became tutors, Zifang became guardian—in end again accomplished.
s0343.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu kept toasting himself toward deposing Liu Ying until the Four Hoary Heads arrived as tutors and Zhang Liang as guardian—then the succession held.

s0344.literal: Before affairs not forgetting, after affairs' warning.
s0344.idiomatic: Remember the past if you would govern the future.

s0345.literal: Meng Ke has saying: 'Orphan minister sinful son, their exercise care also peril, ponder trouble also deep'—therefore much good accomplishment.
s0345.idiomatic: Mencius said that a minister out in the cold and a son born in disgrace 'live on a knife's edge and think hard about peril'—and that is why they often accomplish good.

s0346.literal: Li Si said: 'Kind mother many ruins sons; strict house no shackled captives.
s0346.idiomatic: Li Si wrote, 'Too gentle a mother ruins her boys; in a stern household nobody ends in chains.'

s0347.literal: ' From Your Majesty spoiled Yu causing reach here; perhaps his receiving crime since then, enough self think reform.
s0347.idiomatic: Your Majesty spoiled Yu into this mess; perhaps suffering for it has taught him enough to change.

s0348.literal: Square now Under Heaven many troubles, four barbarians not quiet, generals spy state's crack.
s0348.idiomatic: The realm rustles with trouble, the frontier is restless, and enemies watch for any crack in the wall.

s0349.literal: Heir-support great matter, not appropriate empty void.
s0349.idiomatic: The succession is too vital to leave hollow.

s0350.literal: Ought act great plan, small again pause-stay.
s0350.idiomatic: Plot for the long term and pause before you act.

s0352.literal: Follow Plains Marquis precedent; if not repent-reform, abandon not yet late also.
s0352.idiomatic: Follow Emperor Ming's plain-marquis model; if Yu will not mend his ways, you may still cast him off later.

s0353.literal: Your servant plain cold-gate, no strength office-career, not passed Eastern Palace, feeling not private to Yu.
s0353.idiomatic: I am a nobody from a cold gate with no pull at court; I never served the Eastern Palace. I do not plead for Yu out of private fondness.

s0354.literal: I recall Chu state's virgin admonished her king saying 'Has dragon no tail'—speech year forty, not yet had crown prince.
s0354.idiomatic: I remember the Chu girl who warned her king he was 'a dragon without a tail'—past forty with no heir.

s0355.literal: Your servant once filled near post; although not obtained self-knot Heaven sun, feeling same gate-guard, earnest-earnest sincerity, all for state's plan.
s0355.idiomatic: I once held a post close to the throne; though I never won a private audience, my heart is as exposed as a gatekeeper's—every word is for the dynastic plan.

s0356.literal: Your servant old mother seeing servant make memorial, then for servant divined hexagram, saying 'Writing reaches throne then death.'
s0356.idiomatic: When my mother saw this draft she cast the yarrow for me: 'If the memorial reaches the throne, you die.'

s0357.literal: Wife children detained servant, weeping-tears seeing stop.
s0357.idiomatic: My wife and children clung to me, weeping, begging me to stop.

s0358.literal: Your servant alone thought repeatedly seeing pull-promote, once was near post—this grace hard forget; how repay virtue?
s0358.idiomatic: Yet I have been raised from nothing and once stood near the radiance of the throne; that grace is not forgotten. How else could I repay it?

s0359.literal: Only ought state sincerity, by death offer loyalty.
s0359.idiomatic: I can only speak my mind and offer loyalty unto death.

s0360.literal: Thereupon prepared coffin padding, prostrate await execution-punishment.
s0360.idiomatic: I have coffin and shroud ready and await the executioner's stroke.

s0361.idiomatic: The memorial reached the throne and went unread.

s0362.literal: Reaching Zhang Hua meet harm, Jia Mi meet execution, court wild quaked; Zuan alone stroked Hua corpse wailed, saying: 'Early told you yield post but not willing—now fruit not avoid—fate, ah!
s0362.idiomatic: When Zhang Hua was killed and Jia Mi cut down, the capital shook; Zuan alone cradled Zhang Hua's body and wept, 'I told you to yield your post and you refused—now see what fate costs.'

s0363.literal: Passing rebuked Jia Mi corpse, saying: 'Little boy disorder state's from—execute him late indeed!'
s0363.idiomatic: Passing Jia Mi's corpse he spat, 'You child—this is why the realm burned. They should have killed you sooner.'

s0364.literal: Imperial great-grandson established, Zuan again submitted rough memorial, saying:
s0364.idiomatic: When the imperial great-grandson was named heir, Zuan filed another memorial:

s0365.literal: Your servant before submitted memorial litigate crown prince's wrong, not seen examine-view.
s0365.idiomatic: Your servant once petitioned for the crown prince's innocence; it was never read.

s0366.literal: Formerly Huguan three-old stated Guard crown prince's wrong, yet Han Wu built Thinking-Son terrace.
s0366.idiomatic: The elder of Huguan pleaded for Prince Ju, and Emperor Wu answered by building the Terrace for the Longing Son.

s0367.literal: High Temple director Tian Qianqiu submitted memorial, dared not straight-speak, entrusted with ghosts-spirits teaching—yet Emperor Wu greatly moved, within month thrice promoted, rank reached chancellor, rode carriage entered hall, titled Cart clan.
s0367.idiomatic: Tian Qianqiu, caretaker of Gaozu's shrine, dared not speak plainly and framed his plea as a ghost's warning—yet Emperor Wu was so moved that within a month he promoted him three times to chancellor, let him ride a carriage into the hall, and nicknamed his line the House of the Cart.

s0368.literal: Hate your servant essence-sincerity thin slight, not able have move—end caused crown prince drift-separate, lose life Xuchang.
s0368.idiomatic: I blame my own thin eloquence: I could not move you, and the heir wandered to his death in Xuchang.

s0369.literal: Had ordered Your Majesty immediately accept servant words, not reach this calamity.
s0369.idiomatic: Had you taken my words when I first offered them, this disaster would never have come.

s0370.literal: Heaven assist sage intent, Three Dukes offer stratagem, commoner ordered die, criminal this obtained, crown prince thereby cleared—your servant hates its lateness, nothing again reach.
s0370.idiomatic: Heaven shifted your heart, the Three Dukes plotted, the culprit was ordered to die, the crime was proved, and the crown prince's name was cleared—I mourn only that justice came too late to save him.

s0371.literal: Edict book kind-mourn, welcome bier return bury, restore his ritual-rank—truly matched crowd hope; not expected Lü, Huo change again born at today!
s0371.idiomatic: Your merciful edict welcomed his bier home, restored his rites, and matched what the people wanted—who imagined we would see another Lü or Huo drama in our own day?

s0372.literal: Prostrate see edict establish imperial great-grandson—this truly Your Majesty above follow former canons to calm altars-and-grain, within console kind-mourn wronged souls' pain, below order myriad regions heart have what fastens.
s0372.idiomatic: I see you have proclaimed the great-grandson heir: above, you heed the old pattern and steady the temples; within, you comfort wronged ghosts; below, you give the realm something to cling to.

s0373.literal: Tracing recall commoner-status culprit, deeds without shape, nearly toppled ancestral temple—relied minister-in-chief, grand tutor utmost loyalty rage-rose, covert plots altogether cut, uphold assist sage intent, thereby complete divine martialness.
s0373.idiomatic: Remember the stripped conspirators whose crimes nearly overturned the altars—it took the chief minister's and grand tutor's fierce loyalty and their secret strikes, all in accord with your will, to finish the coup as cleanly as a god of war.

s0374.literal: Although Zhou executed two uncles, Han swept all Lüs—not enough thereby compare.
s0374.idiomatic: Even the Zhou executions of Guan and Cai and Han's massacre of the Lü clan fade beside this righteousness.

s0375.literal: Your servant wishes Your Majesty thereby great further thorough reform—take as lasting regulation.
s0375.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to ride this tide into sweeping reform—write it as permanent statute.

s0376.literal: Ritually install crown prince, dwell by knight ritual, rank with state's people, set official retinue, all like friends, not pure subjects.
s0376.idiomatic: By classical rites the heir should live as a knight among the people; his staff should be friends, not mere vassals.

s0377.literal: Already make above satisfy utmost hope, thereby exalt filial Way; further order not mutually stern-fear, easy mutually regulate-correct.
s0377.idiomatic: That satisfies the court's loftiest hopes and crowns filial duty, yet keeps tutor and pupil from freezing in fear so they can correct one another openly.

s0378.literal: Formerly Han Wu already trusted wicked slander, endangered crown prince; again used qi-watching words, wished exhaust execute edict-prison inmates.
s0378.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Han listened to poison and ruined his heir, then listened to geomancy and meant to butcher every prisoner named in an edict.

s0379.literal: Bing Ji because imperial grandson was there, closed gate resisted mandate; afterward then embraced-guarded imperial grandson, supervised-punish wet-nurse, end reached adult person, established Filial Manifest emperor.
s0379.idiomatic: Bing Ji barred the gate because the imperial grandson was inside, then shielded the boy, disciplined the wet-nurse, and raised him to the throne as Emperor Xuan.

s0380.literal: If resolve at loyalty, nowhere not go-able.
s0380.idiomatic: Where loyalty is the aim, no road is barred.

s0381.literal: Survey-view ancients—although not avoid death—also from generation teaching lenient thereby complete integrity.
s0381.idiomatic: The ancients did not shun death, but their age still forgave enough of it to let integrity stand.

s0382.literal: Ji although resisted edict document, affair lay in loyalty—therefore pardon without blame.
s0382.idiomatic: Bing Ji defied an edict for loyalty's sake—so he was spared and never charged.

s0383.literal: Self Jin rise since, use law too severe; delay-haste between, then add execute behead.
s0383.idiomatic: Since Jin arose the code has swung toward cruelty: hesitate a moment or move too fast and the headsman appears.

s0384.literal: One body submit law, still can force-done; present age's executions, move then exterminate gate.
s0384.idiomatic: A man may force himself through a solo execution, but nowadays a sentence means an exterminated lineage.

s0385.literal: Formerly Empress Lü faced court, wanton conduct no Way.
s0385.idiomatic: Empress Lü held court and indulged every cruelty.

s0386.literal: Zhou Chang chancellor-ed Zhao—thrice summoned its king yet Chang not dispatch—first summoned Chang enter, afterward then summoned king.
s0386.idiomatic: Zhou Chang governed Zhao for the throne: three summonses for the king, and Zhou Chang refused each time until the court called Zhou Chang in first—only then could they summon the king.

s0387.literal: This from Han system root lenient, obtain make it swift.
s0387.idiomatic: Han law was loose enough to allow that boldness.

s0388.literal: Suppose order like today—Empress Lü must say Chang already rebelled, level his three clans—then who again dares act die-for-righteousness!
s0388.idiomatic: Under our code Empress Lü would call it revolt, flatten three clans, and no one would ever die for principle again.

s0389.literal: This law ought reform, can make endure far.
s0389.idiomatic: Change that law if you want the dynasty to last.

s0390.literal: Further Han beginning removed Zhao King Zhang Ao; his subject Guan Gao plotted kill Emperor Gao; Emperor Gao not execute—thereby clarify minister Way.
s0390.idiomatic: Early Han deposed King Zhang Ao of Zhao when his retainer Guan Gao tried to murder Gaozu; Gaozu spared the king to teach what true vassalage means.

s0391.literal: Tian Shu, Meng Shu ten men became slaves, shave-collar followed king, conceal-kin serve nurture—therefore order peace-safe.
s0391.idiomatic: Tian Shu, Meng Shu, and eight others shaved their heads, wore the neck-iron, and followed their lord as slaves to hide and serve him—so he lived.

s0392.literal: Had ordered Jin law obtain contain act righteousness, Eastern Palace ministers obtain like Zhou Chang, firm-guard crown prince obtain like Bing Ji, resist edict not sit crime, prostrate die remonstrate contend—then sage intent must change, crown prince thereby safe.
s0392.idiomatic: Had our statutes blessed such loyalty—had Eastern Palace aides been another Zhou Chang, guardians another Bing Ji, free to defy forged orders and die remonstrating—the throne would have turned and the heir would stand today.

s0393.literal: Like Tian Shu, Meng Shu attend-follow not crime—then conceal-kin left-right, treacherous-villain poison medicine no fate obtain set—crown prince not die young.
s0393.idiomatic: If men like Tian Shu and Meng Shu could attend a disgraced prince without guilt, trusted hands would stay at his side and poisoners would find no seam—no early death for the heir.

s0394.literal: Your servant each blamed Eastern Palace ministers formerly no attend-followers—but afterward heard considerably have at road-watch carriage bow farewell—yet offices seize deliver Luoyang prison, memorialize sentence their crime.
s0394.idiomatic: I condemned the Eastern Palace staff for leaving no companions—then learned many bowed farewell along the roadside and were shackled into Luoyang jail on memorialized charges.

s0395.literal: Yet servant's fellows none followed—indeed had reason thereof.
s0395.idiomatic: Small wonder none of his old friends dared walk with him.

s0396.literal: Further root-set three lieutenants, flourish their infantry-cavalry—thereby night-guard defence watch.
s0396.idiomatic: You stationed the three Household guards and swollen their horses and spears precisely to ward the palace overnight.

s0397.literal: Yet agents abrupt arrive, none had alert strict double-request examine—this from dread fear extinction clan.
s0397.idiomatic: Yet when couriers crashed the gates nobody armed the watch or demanded proof—terror of clan extinction did that.

s0398.literal: Now imperial grandson tender-young, gone affairs many therefore.
s0398.idiomatic: The imperial grandson is a child in a season of fresh disasters.

s0399.literal: If have un-foreseen—strong minister monopolize rule, treacherous-evil fake edict—although have minister-in-chief guard-instruct Eastern Palace, embrace-shield grace same as Bing Ji—only can make jade body peace-safe—ought open come safeguard, can write in statute: from now after, all have abolish-enthronement haste, crowd ministers all obtain then strict-arm, must record bring hall front, face receive mouth edict, afterward count trust—obtain match Zhou Chang not dispatch king tally; below listen subject-son conceal-kin gain like Tian Shu, Meng Shu, not add crime blame—then forever firm heir-support, thereafter secure succession far plan.
s0399.idiomatic: If crisis comes—a strongman's junta, forged edicts—even a Bing Ji at the Eastern Palace saves only flesh. Open permanent safeguards: decree that sudden depositions force every minister to lock the precincts until registers reach the stair and edicts are heard mouth-to-ear; match Zhou Chang's refusal to surrender the tally; forgive hidden service like Tian Shu and Meng Shu. Then the heir survives and the lineage endures beyond our sight.

s0400.literal: Come affairs hard know; gone affairs can reform.
s0400.idiomatic: Tomorrow is unknowable—yesterday can still be mended.
